# Section 5: Administration and Organization

Section 5 addresses institutional administrative structures and the qualifications of administrators.

## Standard 5.1 — Chief Executive Officer [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has a chief executive officer with appropriate authority to lead the institution.

### Typical Evidence Types

- CEO job description
- CEO credentials (CV, transcripts)
- Board delegation of authority
- CEO contract or appointment letter
- Organizational chart

### Suggested Owners

- Board Chair
- Human Resources

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- CEO role unclear or authority limited
- Missing evidence of board delegation
- Interim CEO arrangements not clearly documented

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community college Presidents are selected locally by Boards of Trustees following SBCC policies. Include:

- State Board credential requirements for presidents
- Board policies on presidential selection
- Presidential reporting relationship to Board
:::

---

## Standards 5.2.a-c — CEO Responsibilities

### Standard 5.2.a — Institution Control

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** The CEO has responsibility for institutional control and day-to-day operations.

### Standard 5.2.b — Accreditation Liaison

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** The CEO serves as the institution's accreditation liaison.

### Standard 5.2.c — Personnel Appointments

**What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure:** The CEO has authority over personnel appointments and governance.

### Typical Evidence Types for 5.2

- Board policies delegating authority to CEO
- Job descriptions showing reporting lines
- Accreditation contact documentation
- Personnel policies

---

## Standard 5.3 — Organizational Structure

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has an organizational structure that ensures administration functions properly.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Organizational chart
- Position descriptions for all administrative roles
- Evidence of administrative qualifications

---

## Standard 5.4 — Qualified Administrators

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

All administrators have appropriate credentials and experience for their roles.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Administrator roster with credentials
- Position descriptions with required qualifications
- CVs and transcripts for each administrator

### Suggested Owners

- Human Resources
- Vice Presidents / Deans

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Credentials don't match position requirements
- Missing transcripts or CVs
- Job descriptions without clear requirements

---

## Standard 5.5 — Personnel Appointment Policies

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

Personnel policies govern appointment of staff and administrators.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Personnel policies and procedures manual
- Hiring policies
- Background check policies
- Employee handbook

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges follow both SBCC personnel policies and local board policies. Document both levels of policy and their relationship. Reference relevant SBCC Code provisions.
:::
